definition: Gemma is a series of source-available large language models developed by Google DeepMind.
details: It is based on similar technologies as Gemini. The first version was released in February 2024, followed by Gemma 2 in June 2024, Gemma 3 in March 2025, and the open-weights Gemma 4 in April 2026. Variants of Gemma have also been developed, such as the vision-language model PaliGemma and the model MedGemma for medical consultation topics.

explainer.lead: Gemma is Google DeepMind’s family of large language models, built with technology similar to Gemini. It gives developers a series of text models alongside specialist variants for images and medical consultation topics.

tiers.eli5: Gemma is like a family of very well-read helpers made by Google DeepMind: you give one a written request, and it writes a response. Some family members have special skills, such as PaliGemma working with pictures and words, or MedGemma focusing on medical consultation topics. New versions arrived from February 2024 onward.
tiers.practitioner: Choose a Gemma release for general language work, PaliGemma for vision-language applications, or MedGemma when the application concerns medical consultation topics. Keep version names and dates explicit, because Gemma, Gemma 2, Gemma 3, and Gemma 4 are separate releases. Also distinguish the family’s source-available positioning from the specifically open-weights Gemma 4 release.
tiers.paperLevel: Gemma denotes a series of source-available large language models developed by Google DeepMind using technologies similar to Gemini, rather than one fixed model checkpoint. Its release sequence is Gemma in February 2024, Gemma 2 in June 2024, Gemma 3 in March 2025, and open-weights Gemma 4 in April 2026. PaliGemma and MedGemma extend the family into vision-language modelling and medical consultation topics, respectively.

explainer.example: A developer building an application that answers questions about an image could choose PaliGemma rather than a text-only Gemma model. If the application instead focuses on medical consultation topics, MedGemma is the specialist variant named for that area.

flow: A user supplies a written prompt to a core Gemma language model.
The model processes the request using technology similar to Gemini and generates a text response.
For specialist applications, PaliGemma handles vision-language input, while MedGemma addresses medical consultation topics.
explainer.origin: Google DeepMind developed Gemma and released the first version in February 2024. It is based on technologies similar to those used in Gemini.
explainer.lineage: Gemma 2 followed in June 2024, Gemma 3 in March 2025, and the open-weights Gemma 4 in April 2026. The family also branched into PaliGemma for vision-language work and MedGemma for medical consultation topics.
explainer.whyItMatters: Gemma organizes several Google DeepMind releases and specialist variants under one model family. That makes it possible to select a general language model or a variant aimed at images or medical consultation topics.
